description:
Advances: ancora.derive

Ready-for: investigate

Symptom: after ancora 1.3.4 (special forms dropped, ancora-w5n), calls into imported dependency helpers are the largest remaining group in derived/unresolved_calls. On Argos aa8f738f7 with base aa8f738f7~10, 16,044 distinct unresolved sites remain. console.admin alone has 5,648, and 758 of its 992 tagged tests are still marked incomplete, so Compare can't prove removals for them.

Evidence (measured for PR #12; re-run `MIX_ENV=test mix spec.check --base aa8f738f7~10 --verbose` on an Argos worktree with ancora 1.3.4 as a path dep):
- Top remaining sites: has_element?/2 (2,804), has_element?/3 (2,549), live/2 (1,441), json_response/2 (767), Ecto.Query field/2 (676), type/2 (643), from/2 (569), then element/2, post/3, render_click/1 and more.
- `Ancora.Gate` never passes `external_modules:` to `Derive.context/4`, so `external_exports` is always empty in production.
- Imports injected by `use ConnCase` or `use DataCase` in test support are invisible to the resolver; they surface as `dynamic_module __using__/1`.

Why now: 1.3.4 is published, and Manuel chose to batch the next consumer rollout with this fix, so it gates the 1.3.4 rollout to eight repos.

Suspected cause: the gate has to collect non-member import targets, including those imported inside test support `__using__` blocks, and resolve them against dependency exports without loading target code. ancora.decision.no_execution_no_state forbids executing target code, and the load path never includes the target's `_build`. Any design must keep the resolver pure and must not load the target's compiled modules.
title: Imported dependency helpers fill derived/unresolved_calls
